title: Graded / partial-credit scoring to cut gate variance (SearchQA, OfficeQA, LiveMath): measured negative as a variance lever; useful only as a form-vs-substance diagnostic
purpose: Purpose 2 is the main one: the gate statistic and the evolve-on-one, evaluate-on-the-others metric are the same measurement, and a lower-noise score at equal validity would show transfer with fewer items. There is also a by-product for purpose 1: the same machinery classifies failures as answer FORM versus SUBSTANCE, and that is the executable core of a verification-side "coding rubric".
verdict_cn:
结论：可行性低。实测结果基本是否定的：部分得分不能降低门槛的噪声，有些还会奖励错的东西。

要解决的问题：现在的"门槛"（判断一条新学到的规则能否被接受的统计检验）只看每道题对还是错。同一段提示词原样重跑一次，约16%的题目对错会翻转，噪声很大。设想是改用"部分得分"：答案接近正确也给一部分分。看这样能否让噪声变小，用更少的题分辨出真正有用的规则。

我做了什么：
- 数据：用已经跑完的校准实验（cal-1：11种提示词，每种在同样200道 SearchQA 训练题上各答4次，共8,800个答案），以及第三版协议完整运行（v3）中训练阶段的答案。SearchQA 是检索问答，OfficeQA 是文档数字问答，LiveMath 是数学选择题。
- 打分方式：设计并计算了十几种。机械规则有：去掉 JSON 外壳再比对；"标准答案外最多多3个词"也算对；按词重合度给分。另外让另一个大模型 GLM-5.3 当评审，判断答案的意思对不对（每个不同的答案问3次，取多数）。
- 花费：共用约132万个 GLM 词元（token，模型计费单位），没有调用解题模型。
- 全程只用训练题，没碰任何测试题。

主要发现：
1. 和官方打分比较。官方打分叫"完全匹配"（EM）：答案规范化后要和标准答案一字不差才算对。
   - 部分得分从不把官方判对的答案判错，只是给官方判错的答案加分。
   - GLM 评审认为，官方判错的答案里有75%（2,767个中的2,076个）意思其实是对的，只是写法不对，比如多了解释、包了一层 JSON、用了别名。
   - 我人工抽查，这些"意思对"的判断大约87%到93%站得住。
2. 噪声。同一段提示词跑两次的差别，用部分得分确实小一些；但和题与题之间的差别相比，只小了一点。
3. 最关键的一点：有一段已知有效的提示词，即任务说明卡，比空白提示多答对9.3个百分点。要把它和空白提示分开，没有哪种部分得分能稳定地少用题。
   - 最好的两种是"官方对得1分、意思对但写法错得0.5分"和"按词重合度给分"。它们只省10%到15%的题，而且误差范围里包含"更差"。
   - 宽松打分和纯评审打分，反而要多用1.7到8倍的题。
   - 原因：在 SearchQA 上，噪声和真实效果主要都来自答案的写法。同一提示词前后不一致的情况中，83%到87%只是写法变化；有效提示词带来的提升，64%也是写法变好。放宽写法要求，就把噪声和效果一起抹掉了。
4. 奖励错东西的风险，已实际测到。
   - 我把 v3 的13次门槛判决用新打分重新算了一遍；用官方打分重算时，与原记录完全一致。
   - 如果改用"意思对给半分"、"去掉外壳再比"或"宽松"打分，v3 里被拒绝的那条规则（E-ds 链第1阶段第1条；E-ds 是从空白提示开始进化的那条链）就会通过。
   - 但校准实验用全部200题测量，这条规则让官方分数下降2.6个百分点（误差范围从下降7.2到上升2.0）；在"给半分"的打分下也是零效果。
5. 另外两个数据集。
   - OfficeQA："误差1%以内算对"看起来好一些，但这会把查错行、查错年份的数（比如把 501 当成 498）算成对。只接受四舍五入后相等的严格版本，没有任何改进。
   - LiveMath：数据里只有选项字母，没有部分得分可给。
6. 还发现一个更大的噪声来源。完全相同的请求，在相隔16小时的两次运行里，空白提示的正确率差了6.1个百分点。任何打分方式都消除不了，只能靠"同一时段内交错运行各组"来避免。

建议：
- 门槛和所有测试结论，继续用官方的对/错打分，不改成部分得分。门槛共有四条标准：C1 是在目标题上有收益；C2 是不伤害其余题；C3 是不伤害以前学过的数据集；C4' 是不伤害相似的数据集。
- 增加一层"写法问题还是内容问题"的分类，只用于诊断，不参与决策。它由三部分组成：
  - 程序检查：有没有答案标签、有没有 JSON 外壳、字数多少；
  - 在训练题上对照标准答案的宽松匹配；
  - 固定版本的 GLM 评审，结果存起来重复使用。
  成本约为解题花费的2%到5%。它服务两个目的：
  - 目的1（协同进化）：让验证端告诉提规则的模型"这条规则的损失全在写法上"。
  - 目的2（跨数据集泛化）：分清分数提升是"写法迁移"还是"知识迁移"。
- 所谓"编码评分细则"（验证端的检查规则），更适合做成可执行的程序检查，再逐步增加检查项。大模型评审的部分要按版本固定，否则不同版本的分数没法比较。
- 降低噪声的力气应该花在其他探索方向上：D1 是每一步换一批新题来验收；D5 是降低测量噪声，比如同一时段交错运行；D8 是完善统计流程，比如更多题目和次数。
what_i_did:
1. Read context.md and context-batch2.md.
2. Extracted the complete cal-1 SearchQA unit (8,800 cells; attempt-1 7,189 + attempt-2 1,611) read-only from the old machine. Extracted all v3 training-side cells of stages s1-s3 (train/screen/confirm, both chains; 10,178 rows) and the recorded gate verdicts and prepared rules from the new machine. Pinned training gold only; forbidden-path asserts throughout.
3. Re-implemented the official scorers. They reproduce all 8,777 stored cal-1 verdicts and metrics, and the registered C1 arithmetic (0.756 vs 0.7575).
4. Built the graded scores:
   - SearchQA: format-robust EM, lenient (gold + <= 3 words), token F1, substring, a mechanical ladder, a GLM-5.3 3-vote equivalence judge (CORRECT/PARTIAL/WRONG), em_half (1 if EM, else 0.5 x judge-correct), and a GLM 3-criterion rubric (TYPE/ENTITY/SPECIFIC).
   - OfficeQA: last-number relative error, numerically equal, sig-fig/year-safe, within 1%, scale error, ladder.
   - LiveMath: letter validity and robust letter.
5. Measured on cal-1 (attempt-1 and full):
   - (a) boundary agreement and kappa with EM;
   - (b) the same-text noise floor parent:B - parent:A (sd, sd/spread, retest r, flip rates, ICC);
   - (c) separation of ids-full from parent:A: dz, SNR, analytic and simulated n80, a NaN-safe item bootstrap of n80 ratios, and C1-type passage on the registered pools at matched null thresholds.
6. Decomposed noise and signal into form vs substance with the judge. Hand-audited 56 judge decisions.
7. Measured between-session drift for byte-identical requests and within-session time effects.
8. Replayed all 13 recorded v3 gate verdicts under each score. To do so I judged the 173 v3 gate answer pairs missing from the cache.
9. Measured how far gold-free executable checks (the v3 examiner rubric's R1-R3, plus JSON wrapper etc.) predict the official verdict.
10. Surveyed partial-credit, answer-equivalence and rubric-scoring literature.
11. Wrote the report and mirrored all scripts and outputs.
evidence:
All figures are MEASURED on training-side cells. Unless stated, they use the full cal-1 data (199 items with every score).

(a) Boundary agreement with official EM:
- No graded score fails an EM pass: 0 of 6,008.
- Format-robust EM passes 327 of 2,777 EM failures (kappa 0.911); lenient 1,083 (0.681); F1>=0.5 1,585 (0.507).
- The GLM judge rates 2,076 of 2,767 EM failures CORRECT (75.0%; kappa 0.313).
  - By category: wrapper 324/324, lenient 711/759, token overlap 883/995, no overlap 158/681.
- Single-auditor precision of those CORRECT labels: about 87-93% (estimate; 56 pairs).
  - No-overlap class: only 4-5 of 16 defensible (e.g. TGV for trains, giblet gravy for giblets).

(b) Same-text noise floor, sd(B-A)/item spread, full data:
- EM 0.334; F1 0.320; em_half 0.265; ladder 0.264; judge 0.209 (it rests on 6-7 discordant items).
- EM run-paired cell flip rate 0.114.

(c) ids-full vs parent:A. EM +0.093 (46/13 items), SNR 0.612, analytic n80 33. Bootstrap n80 ratio to EM [95%]:
- em_half 0.85 [0.52, 1.32]; F1 0.88 [0.43, 1.42]; em_rob 1.06 [0.86, 1.35].
- Ladder 1.69 [0.89, 7.65]; judge 1.83 [0.51, 18.2]; rubric 2.17 [0.68, 30.2]; lenient 2.45 [1.13, 23.9]; ENTITY=2 8.13 [1.42, inf].
- Simulated grid at 80% power: EM 40, F1 30, em_half 30, judge 50, lenient 60, rubric 60, ENTITY=2 120.
- Registered pool (i), n=11, matched-null power: EM 0.832 (actual null 1.6%), F1 0.881 (5.0%), em_half 0.894 (3.5%), judge 0.857, ladder 0.645, lenient 0.513.

Form vs substance:
- Same-text EM-discordant A/B pairs: the failing side is judge-CORRECT in 75/90 (83%).
- Within-arm EM flips: failing side CORRECT in 1,145/1,320 (86.7%). Semantic flips are 2.5% of pairs.
- ids-full's EM gain is 36% semantic (+0.034 of +0.093).
- cand: EM -0.028 but semantic +0.020 (11/7, n.s.), with form failures 23.0% -> 27.6%.

Wrong-thing risk:
- cand under em_rob +0.068, lenient +0.032, judge +0.020.
- Pool (i), n=11, matched-null pass for cand: EM 0.107 -> em_rob 0.431, judge 0.621, em_half 0.274.
- v3 gate replay: EM reproduces all 13 recorded C1 gains/margins and C2 deltas exactly.
  - Under em_half, em_rob or lenient, E-ds s1-r1 (= cal-1 cand) passes confirm (em_half C1 1.00, C2 -2.75; em_rob C1 2.25, C2 +6.0; lenient C1 1.25, C2 +1.0).
  - Its 200-item effect: official -0.026 [-0.072, +0.020]; em_half -0.004.
  - Under F1, lenient or ladder, I-ds s1-r2 passes screen (effect unknown). No OfficeQA/LiveMath rule passes under any score.

OfficeQA (74 items x 2 runs x 2 chains):
- I-E EM +0.047 [-0.016, +0.110], SNR 0.226, n80 149.
- Within 1%: +0.081 [-0.001, +0.163], SNR 0.330, n80 76. It rewards wrong values (501 vs 498).
- Sig-fig/year-safe: SNR 0.199, n80 186.

LiveMath:
- Census: 141 pass, 251 wrong letter, 7 untagged.
- em_rob = EM; there are no partial-credit fields.

Drift: byte-identical empty-scaffold requests, cal-1 minus v3 train, 16 h apart:
- EM -0.061 (12/38, sign p 0.0003); ladder -0.034; sub_em -0.018 (n.s.).
- Seeded text -0.001.
- Within cal-1 (4 h): late-early -0.008 +- 0.012. Disagreement does not grow with the dispatch gap (EM |diff| 0.090-0.110 over 13,155 pairs).

Executable checks:
- v3 rubric R1|R2|R3 flag 963/2,777 EM failures (34.7%) and 513/6,008 passes (8.5%, all from the no-tag fallback); balanced accuracy 0.631.
- 84% of the flagged failures are judge-CORRECT.
design:
1. Keep official binary scores as the only gate statistic (C1, C2, C3, C4') and as the only test metric. Do not adopt a graded C1.

2. Add a per-cell scoring layer stored beside the official verdict (pure, version-stamped functions as in e6score.py):
   - SearchQA: EM, em_rob, lenient, F1, and format flags (tag present, number of tags, JSON wrapper, answer words, hedge).
   - OfficeQA: EM, relative error of the last number, numerically-equal, rounding <= 0.5%, scale error, year flag.
   - LiveMath: EM and letter validity.

3. Frozen semantic judge for SearchQA EM failures only:
   - the v1 equivalence prompt, or a PEDANTS/SimpleQA-style tightening of it, frozen by hash;
   - 3 votes, majority, cached per (item, normalised answer);
   - EM passes skip the judge (0 of 6,008 EM passes were judged non-correct);
   - a missing label counts as EM for a rule arm and as judge-correct for parent and controls.

4. Per arm and round, give the examiner and analyst a form/substance report (purpose 1): EM change split into form failures (EM fail, judge correct) and substance failures (judge wrong), plus format counts. Example: cal-1 cand = substance +16 cells, form -38 cells, 118 JSON-wrapped answers. The analyst can then repair the form side or drop a form-only rule.

5. Read the "coding rubric" as an executable check set that grows across versions (JSON wrapper, several tags, > k words, numeric scale, letter validity). The LLM part stays frozen per protocol version. Archived cells are re-scored when it changes.

6. Transfer tables (purpose 2): every cross-benchmark delta is reported with its form/substance split.

7. If a graded gate is still wanted, em_half only, as a new pre-registered protocol version:
   - MIN_GAIN and TOLERANCE_FOCAL recalibrated from a same-session parent:A/parent:B null round per benchmark (EM's same-text sd scales by about 0.57x under em_half);
   - a focal-panel format guard (the C3 violation count extended to trigger + rest);
   - the 13 v3 verdicts replayed as a negative control.

8. Variance reduction is handled by design, not scoring: interleaved same-session arms, more items and runs (D5/D8), fresh batches (D1). Every round carries a same-session null pair, because the null shifts between sessions.

pilot.result: GLM-5.3 judge pilot on training items only; no solver calls; nothing blocked. It produced 3-vote equivalence labels for all 542 distinct cal-1 answer pairs, 2-vote rubric scores for 538 pairs, and labels for the 173 v3 gate pairs missing from the cache. Judge repeatability: 89.1% unanimous over 3 votes; rubric all-criteria agreement over 2 votes 78.8%; the two prompts agree 91.8% (binary). 29 votes failed persistently with HTTP 400. All analyses built on these labels are in the report: no graded score reduces the items needed for the positive control; format-forgiving scores need 1.7-8x more items; the v3 replay under em_half, em_rob or lenient confirms one rule (E-ds s1-r1) whose 200-item official effect is -0.026 [-0.072, +0.020].
pilot.command: (1) Earlier incarnation, new machine, proxy on: python judge.py --out /data/feasibility/E6/judge.jsonl --votes 3 --workers 6 (1,545 calls, 614,905 tokens). (2) nohup bash -ic 'proxy_on >/dev/null 2>&1; /data/feasibility/E6/v2/run_judges.sh' > /data/feasibility/E6/v2/out/judges.log 2>&1 & (v1 fill 84 calls + rubric 1,107 calls incl. smoke/retries = 497,571 tokens; plus 13 retry calls, 382 tokens). (3) cd /data/feasibility/E6/v2 && nohup bash -ic "proxy_on >/dev/null 2>&1; /root/continual-alf-prep-20260928/env/bin/python judge_v3cells.py --workers 6" > out/judge_v3cells.log 2>&1 & (519 calls, 211,617 tokens). Concurrency 6; first call checked before release.

risks:
1. Goodhart through format (measured). Forgiving scores turn format-breaking texts (cand, seed-rule3, control:3) into apparent gains. The v3 replay shows one false confirmation under em_half, em_rob or lenient.
2. Judge leniency on related entities. Only 4-5 of 16 no-overlap CORRECT pairs are defensible; overall precision for EM failures is about 87-93% (single auditor).
3. Judge nondeterminism and gaps: 10.9% of pairs are non-unanimous at temperature 0, and 29 votes fail persistently with HTTP 400. Caching makes labels deterministic per answer string, but any judge or provider change rescales the measurement.
4. Judge exploitability (documented master-key false positives). Any judge-based gate becomes an optimisation target for the analyst.
5. OfficeQA relative-tolerance credit rewards different document values. Substring, F1 and lenient scores credit lists and hedges.
6. Comparability: every frozen baseline and v3 result is official EM. A graded protocol needs a new version and output directory and cannot relabel old runs.
7. Limits of this study:
   - one benchmark with a fully crossed design (SearchQA);
   - one strong positive control (seed-only is nearly the same text as ids-full);
   - discrete-vs-continuous null thresholds only approximately matched (EM's actual false-pass 1.6% vs 3.5-5.0%);
   - small, session-confounded OfficeQA/LiveMath contrasts (74/100 items).
8. Unknowns: whether a stricter judge prompt fixes related-entity leniency; whether the PJLAB route returns token probabilities (LiveMath continuous score); the full-panel effects of E-ds s1-r3 and I-ds s1-r2.
cost_estimate:
This exploration: 1,324,475 GLM-5.3 tokens (3,268 calls, about 405 tokens per call); 0 deepseek tokens.

Recommended diagnostic layer:
- 3 votes per new distinct (item, answer) pair. About 6% of cells are new pairs in a cal-1-sized round (542/8,785), so about 0.65M GLM tokens per 8,800-cell round, i.e. about 74 tokens per solver cell.
- That is 2.4% of the ledger-charged solver tokens (cal-1 ledger 27,481,897) or 4.6% of receipt-reported prompt+completion tokens (14.0M).
- At v3 scale (139M tokens), roughly 3-6M GLM tokens (estimate). It falls over time because the cache is reused across arms, rounds and steps.
- Mechanical checks are free.

If em_half were adopted anyway:
- the same judge cost;
- one same-session parent:A/parent:B null round per benchmark (200 items x 4 runs x 2 arms = 1,600 cells, about 5.4M ledger tokens at about 3,400 per cell) to recalibrate MIN_GAIN and the tolerances.

Optional LiveMath gold-letter probability pilot: about 400 cells x 3,400 = 1.4M tokens, only if the route returns logprobs (unverified).
recommendation:
1. Do not use graded or judge scores in C1/C2/C3/C4' or in any test claim. Keep official binary scores. On cal-1, no graded score robustly lowers the items needed for the positive control, and on the v3 replay graded gates confirm a rule with a null or negative 200-item effect.
2. Build the form/substance diagnostic layer: executable checks, gold-based em_rob/lenient on training items, and a frozen cached 3-vote GLM judge. Feed it to the examiner and analyst (purpose 1). Report it beside every cross-benchmark delta, so answer-form transfer is not read as knowledge transfer (purpose 2).
3. Treat the executable part as the evolving "coding rubric" (add checks per version). Freeze the LLM judge per protocol version.
4. Put variance-reduction effort into D5/D8/D1. Same-text noise is 83-87% answer-form flips, which every EM-anchored score keeps. The largest measured shift is between sessions (-6.1 EM points for byte-identical requests 16 h apart), which no score removes. Always compare arms within one interleaved session, with a same-session null pair.
5. Only if the owner insists on a graded gate: pre-register em_half as a new protocol version with a focal format guard, per-benchmark recalibration of MIN_GAIN and the tolerances, and the 13-verdict v3 replay as a negative control.
